prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: concussion. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1195; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of the parking lot collision came in from the insured, who describes a low-speed impact while backing out of a space. The driver is named on the policy, and the insured has agreed to make the vehicle available for inspection.

Entry 2: Photos from the insured show rear-end damage that fits the described impact, though they do not settle every detail. No independent witnesses to the collision have come forward.

Entry 3: The police report lists the claimant as an occupant of the other vehicle, which matches the account given so far. The claimant is now represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 4: The claimant's attorney submitted a demand alleging a concussion from the impact. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this kind.

Entry 5: The medical records show treatment that ran somewhat longer than is usual for this injury. I have requested the full treatment notes and therapy logs to understand the timeline.

Entry 6: No earlier injury to the same body area appears in the records received so far. I will confirm this once the prior provider list is complete.

Entry 7: The claimant has told the same account in every conversation with me and with counsel present. The details have not shifted between contacts.

Entry 8: No earlier damage to the claimant's vehicle is known, and the repair estimate matches the impact that was described. Nothing in the file suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.

Entry 9: Policy review confirms that coverage was active at the time of loss and that the driver is named on the policy. The file stays open pending the treatment records and the final repair invoice.
